title: What If a Killer Smog Trapped a City for 5 Days?

scenes.text: What if a fog trapped a whole city for five days? In 1952, it happened.
In December 1952, a high-pressure system stalled over London and trapped coal smoke close to the ground.
By December 7th, visibility fell to about five yards in many places.
People outside could not see their own feet, and abandoned cars sat in the road.
About 4,000 people died in those five days. Later estimates reach about 12,000.
The killer was ordinary coal fires. Britain banned smoke in the City in 1954, and passed the Clean Air Act in 1956.
